idea: Replace the random-order baseline with a target-similarity filter. (1) Fit a TWF/mean-tokenizer word-bigram (or char n-gram) hash feature map on target_sample, hashed with zlib/adler32 so features are unique keyed strings. (2) For each pool doc, compute the fraction of its first ~2000 characters found in the set of all target-level bigrams; this is "target-likeness" and penalises word-shuffled docs, spam, code, web junk and off-domain text (e.g. Q&A vs WikiText style). (3) Add cheap guards: drop exact/near duplicates (hash of whitespace-normalised text or hash of the first 500 chars), drop docs under 200 characters, drop docs with spam markers ("on all", "free shipping", "click here", "order", coupon patterns). (4) Rank the survivors by target-likeness, and take the top-scoring docs until their estimated token count (len/4, or tiktoken gpt2 if time allows) reaches about T. (5) Shuffle the selected indices with random.Random(int(os.environ.get("CURATE_SEED", 0))) and return them; if the docs that pass the spam/duplicate guards are shorter than T, still fill up to T with the highest-scoring surviving docs rather than using a raw-cycled pool.
why: The pool visibly mixesWikiText-style articles with word-shuffled articles, spam, code, Q&A and off-domain web text, all of which teach the model wrong word order and style, so spending the full T-token budget on intact target-like documents instead of a random half-junk mix should lower held-out bpb substantially.
outcome: dev 2.0159 against 1.9412 for the best at the time, rejected

idea: Add character-level damage detection and class-balance control, on top of the existing spam/duplicate guards. (1) Still compute target-likeness as the fraction of a doc's first ~3000 characters (hashing each adjacent character pair over zlib/adler32) found in the target-sample bigram set; keep the current ranking and selection up to about T tokens. (2) Add two new guards: (a) word-shuffled docs, which the existing bigram score cannot catch wholesale: compute, per doc, the ratio of its most frequent word to the second most frequent word within its first 4000 characters (using UTF-8 text, lowercase and whitespace normalise), and drop docs below a threshold chosen held-out from target_sample — on the 200 target docs take each word's frequency among all target words, build the same statistic on them, and set the limit at half the 5th percentile of that target distribution; also drop docs whose bigram-score is less than half of the 5th percentile of the target bises-me (the mean target-level bigram-hit fraction). (b) character-corrupted filler docs that look like wiki text but are letter-scrambled: build the set of character bigrams seen in target_sample, and for each doc compute the fraction of its character bigrams (first 3000 chars) that are in that set; note that clean target docs score near 1 while shuffled-text docs score near 0.3-0.4. Calibrate by comparing a seeded random sample of 2000 pool docs against the same statistic on the target docs, using the midpoint of the target gap, and keep only docs above it. Use each doc's full text for these counts, not just the prefix. (3) When the docs that pass all guards come to fewer than T tokens, no longer just fill with the next-highest-scoring docs. Shrink the selection: keep the top-scoring docs that pass the guards, plus paid-in demons of other documents — unselected pool docs, ranked by target-likeness, each counted once toward the token budget at half weight and shuffled in, so the trainer sees every retained doc roughly half the time. This lifts the learned word-order prior on chars from outside the target style and detaches the portion of the budget from a single-mode, improbable corpus. (4) Shuffle the final list with random.Random(int(os.environ.get("CURATE_SEED", 0))) and return it.
why: The pool is about twice the budget and is visibly half spam, code, web junk and word-shuffled or character-corrupted wiki text, whereas the target is clean, in-domain, word-order-correct articles, so spending all T tokens on undamaged, in-domain text well-beyond the target style should cut bpb more than any dedup-only or bigram-score-only approach.
outcome: dev 2.0010 against 1.9412 for the best at the time, rejected

idea:
Rewrite the bigram target-likeness filter with a character-bigram set built from the whole target sample, compute it on each doc's full text, and add word-order sanctity checks to catch substitutex, homoglyph and letter-shift damaged docs (the previous two attempts scored above even though they were damaged in small form, unchanged by a 3000-char prefix).

(1) Fit: c = the set of lowercased adjacent character bigrams in target_sample, counted over the full text, keyed by a zlib hash so it fits in memory.

(2) Score: for each pool doc, h = the fraction of its character bigrams (full text, no thresholding) that are in c. Cloze-style wiki text should score near 1; shuffled or letter-scrambled docs score near 0; spam/code fall in between.

(3) Calibrate: split target_sample into two halves, build c on one half and score the other, then switch. Let lo = the midpoint of the 2.5th-95th percentile of those half-half scores and hi = the midpoint of the 5th-95th percentile. Keep a doc if h >= lo AND h >= hi; the second condition removes docs that are partially clean and partially damaged.

(4) Word-order sanctity: with full_text_words = the lowercased whitespace tokens of the full text:
(a) mean_freq = the mean, over tokens, of log1p(word_frequency in full_text_words).
(b) external_freq = the mean, over tokens, of log1p(word_frequency in the word frequency of the whole target_sample).
(c) coherence = 1 - external_freq/mean_freq, clipped at 0.
Clean wiki docs should have coherence >= 0.9; shuffled or homoglyph docs fall short. Set the limit at 0.85.

(5) Select: count tokens as len(text)/4, then with tiktoken gpt2 if time permits. Take all kept docs, sorted by descending h, and keep from the top until roughly T tokens are reached. If the kept set holds fewer than T tokens, output only that set and let it cycle.

(6) Shuffle the final list with random.Random(int(os.environ.get("CURATE_SEED", 0))) and return it.
why: Shuffled-text damage and other subtle corruptions likely comprise a large share of the pool, and the source-domain word-bigram filter only saw a 3000-character prefix, so replacing it with a full-text character-bigram literal hit rate against the actual target, plus an external-word-frequency coherence check, should remove far more junk than the previous attempts.
outcome: dev 1.9009 against 1.9412 for the best at the time, KEPT as the new best

idea: Add a whitespace-corrupted guard and a class-balance check, on top of the existing character-bigram filter (attempt 3). (1) Still compute h, the fraction of adjacent character bigrams in each doc's full text that are in c, the lowercased character-bigram set built from the target sample. Also compute w, the fraction of lowercased whitespace tokens that are in the set of lowercased whitespace tokens of target_sample. (2) Calibrate both at the same time: split the target sample into two halves, build the respective sets on one half and score the other, then switch. Let lo and hi be the half-sample midpoint values as before. Mark a doc clean if h >= lo and h >= hi and both w >= hi and w >= lo. Full-word-shuffled docs, which passed the previous guards, should now fail the w check against the external token set. (3) Add a spam guard as well: lowercase and split the full text, and drop any doc that has more than 3% of its tokens in the set {"on", "of", "to", "in", "for", "and", "the", "a", "an", "at", "by", "with", "from"} or that contains "free shipping", "click here", "order" or "coupon". (4) Count tokens as len(text)/4, with tiktoken gpt2 if time permits. Take the clean survivors, sorted by descending h, and keep from the top until roughly T tokens are reached; if they hold fewer than T, output only that set and let it cycle. (5) Shuffle the final list with random.Random(int(os.environ.get("CURATE_SEED", 0))) and return it.
why: Partial-word-shuffled or character-corrupted wiki-style articles (homoglyph, letter-shift) passed attempt 3's bigram filter, so they probably account for much of the remaining gap from 1.9009 to the raw baseline, and removing them should be the single best remaining factor.
outcome: dev 4.1654 against 1.9009 for the best at the time, rejected

idea: Switch from the surviving-docs-only mode of attempt 3 to a true 50/50 half-butterfly split, since rule (3) already gave 1.9009 with only clean docs and still cycled the same 50% over 300 steps as the random-order baseline before the selection was shuffled. (1) Fit exactly as in attempt 3: c = the set of lowercased adjacent character bigrams in target_sample, keyed by zlib hash, built on the full text. Let h = the fraction of each pool doc's full-text character bigrams that are in c. Calibrate as in attempt 3 with the half-half leave-out, using both the 2.5th-95th midpoint lo and the 5th-95th midpoint hi, and keep a doc if h >= lo and h >= hi. (2) Make no word-order rules; let the raw h separate clean from shuffled, and rank the kept docs by descending h. (3) Split the kept docs into two halves by hash of the first 200 chars: A is the first half, B is the second. Assign IDs: A gets a label "0" with weight 2, B gets a label "1" with weight 2. The externally unlabelled docs outside the kept set are all label "none" with weight 1. (4) Train a logistic regression with positives = the 100 target_sample docs (labels 0/1) and negatives = a seeded 3000-doc random sample of the pool (CURATE_SEED), weight = the labels above. Score every pool doc; the decision is the midpoint between the 5th percentile of the target scores and the 95th percentile of the held-out pool scores. A doc is kept if its score is above the midpoint, regardless of label. (5) Among kept docs, form the selection as far as possible from A (weight 2); if A alone holds fewer than T tokens at weight 2, top up with B (weight 2) until T is reached, so A and B are learned about half the time each. If even the kept A docs hold fewer than T tokens at weight 2, still use only kept docs and let them cycle. (6) Shuffle the final list with random.Random(int(os.environ.get("CURATE_SEED", 0))) and return it.
why: The baseline learned a word-order prior from 1000 seen docs per step while only half the budget was backing it up with clean external text, so spending the whole T budget on a half-shuffled wiki copy (the other half is the held-out target) cannot do worse than rule 3's single-mode cycle, and a learned classifier should mix kept clean outside far more than the raw-order guess.
outcome: dev 1.8826 against 1.9009 for the best at the time, KEPT as the new best

idea: Replace the half-butterfly shuffle of attempt 5 with a deduplicated full-corpus pass, so every clean doc that fits is seen roughly once and only score相似的极富重复性的 wiki 文档被重复多次。(1)Exact and near duplicate removal: for each pool doc normalise by lowercasing, whitespace split and collapsing runs of whitespace to one, and truncate to its first 4000 characters, compute the hash of the whitespace-encoded text (size matters, not sequence), and keep only the first doc per hash. Also drop docs under 200 characters.(2)Damage filter: build c as the lowercased character bigram set from target_sample (full text), and for each pool doc compute h as the fraction of its full-text character bigrams in c, without prefix limits, no thresholding; keep docs with h >= lo, where lo is the half-half leave-out 2.5th-95th percentile midpoint as before (no hi, since attempt 3 with hi gave 4.1654 when there was nothing to fill with).(3)Selection: count tokens with tiktoken gpt2. Sort the kept docs by descending h. Take docs from the top until about T tokens are reached. If the kept set holds fewer than T tokens, still use only that set and let it cycle. Keep at most 3000 docs; the only repetition is the cycle relationally natural one. Count a doc in tokens as len(enc.encode_ordinary_300k(doc)), or with a strong lower-bound if time is short: max(500, len(doc)/4), and coerce a truncated final doc to its whole text by appending ' ' + the first 200 characters of the next kept doc so the doc is never split across selection steps.(4)Shuffle with random.Random(int(os.environ.get("CURATE_SEED", 0))) and return the list. No split, no weights, no external negatives, no fillers.
why: Attempt 5's best score came with a small surviving set, so a deduplicated, top-h selected set that is actually larger than before should teach each window of the model on more varied clean text only once, rather than only half of it twice.
outcome: dev 1.9006 against 1.8826 for the best at the time, rejected

idea: Deduplicate more thoroughly and add a space-adjusted target set, on top of attempt 6. (1) Exact duplicate removal: for each pool doc, normalise uniquely by lowercasing, whitespace collapse, and keeping only the first 2000 characters, then hash the whitespace-encoded bytes; keep only the first doc per hash. (2) Near duplicate removal: build the set of all suffixes of length up to 200 characters over the vocabulary of target_sample tokens (lowercased whitespace tokens) using the first 4000 characters of each pool doc, keyed by zlib hash of the suffix plus a delimiter byte. Count how many other docs share each suffix. Drop a doc if the number of other docs sharing at least 5% of its suffixes is more than 2 × its own copy-count, and absorb the drop into the top-ranked survivor by checksum of the first 300 bytes. (3) Character damage: keep docs with h >= lo, as in attempt 6, with no hi. (4) Token count is max(500, len(enc.encode_ordinary_300k(doc))) with a final doc by appending ' ' + the first 200 characters of the next kept doc; do not truncate any doc. (5) Selection is the kept docs sorted by descending h, stopped at about T tokens; if they hold fewer than T, let them cycle and do not add off-domain fillers. If there are fewer than 100 kept docs, fall back to the clean top-h scored docs as in attempt 6. (6) Shuffle with random.Random(int(os.environ.get('CURATE_SEED', 0))) and return the list. No split, no weights, nothing external.
why: Attempt 6 most likely spent its T-token budget on a small set of repeated clean wiki docs rather than on a full diverse domain, and a target-or-bigram hash keyed only by bytes cannot see a second copy pasted with different whitespace, title casing or encoding, so the surge in coverage should be the next biggest gain.
outcome: dev 2.3408 against 1.8826 for the best at the time, rejected

idea: Swap the shuffle-from-behind selection of attempt 5 for a full-corpus, ranked selection, since attempts 6 and 7 show that documentation, and分销 not damaged. (1) Damage filter: keep docs with h >= lo, exactly as in attempt 5, written on the half-half leave-out 2.5th-95th midpoint with no hi. (2) Deduplicate: exact duplicates by lowercasing and hashing the first 2000 characters (keep the first copy only), plus near duplicates: build the set of lowercased whitespace tokens that occur at least 2 times in target_sample, and for each pool doc compute the fraction of its first 4000 tokens that are in that set, then use a transducer score that compares the token bigram frequency profile against the target profile (log of conditional bigram rate divided by the log of the geometric mean of the unigram rate and the target unigram rate, with a 2nd-order trigram-bigram leave-one-out bigram baseline); drop a doc if its rate rank relative to the 2nd-order held-out downgrades it to below half the 5th percentile of that target distribution, and absorb the drop into the highest-checked survivor by line checksum of the first 300 bytes. (3) Token count is max(500, len(enc.encode_ordinary_300k(doc))). (4) Selection is the kept docs sorted by descending h, taken from the top until about T tokens are reached. If the kept set holds fewer than T, let it cycle only; do not add off-domain fillers. (5) Shuffle with random.Random(int(os.environ.get('CURATE_SEED', 0))) and return the list. No split, no weights, nothing external.
why: Attempts 2 and 3 compared shuffling-up-made docs with the raw-target-order baseline, and attempt 5's learned target order beat the shuffle as measured by held-out bpb, so a deduplicated, highest-h-first, wholly-clean pass should be at least as good as the half-butterfly when it is no longer fetching clean docs by score and mixing them with junk.
outcome: dev 1.9047 against 1.8826 for the best at the time, rejected

idea: Lighten the damage filter so it lets through word-shuffled and letter-scrambled docs that scored in attempt 3, since attempt 7's drop rate to 'about half the 5th percentile of the target distribution' is far larger than the half-half leave-out gap used for lo, and the kept set is now known to be far smaller than 2T, so there is plenty of room to fill with outside text. (1) Calibrate once on the whole sample: build c from 80% of target_sample and score the 20% held-out, then swap; let target_median be the median of full-text h over all 200 target docs, and lo be the 5th percentile of the held-out scores. (2) Keep all pool docs with h >= 0.5 × lo and h >= 0.5 × target_median. No hi; no near-duplicate removal. Do not shuffle the pool before scoring: score 3000 docs with full text, then 3000 docs with only the first 6000 characters, and obviously the 6000-char half gives a higher h, so the 0.5 × lo limit leaves the 3000-char half, as it should. (3) Token count is len(enc.encode_ordinary_300k(doc)), with the final doc padded as before. (4) Selection is the kept docs sorted by descending h, taken from the very top until about T tokens are reached. Because the kept set now holds far fewer tokens than the unlabelled pool—as shown by the wide jump from 1.9009 to 2.3408 when it was shrink-wrapped—if the kept docs hold fewer than T tokens, let them cycle and do not add unbuffered off-domain fillers, and do not rescore the extra tokens as existing docs do not have order labels, since only clean target-style text feeds the target prior. (5) Shuffle with random.Random(int(os.environ.get('CURATE_SEED', 0))) and return the list.
why: Attempt 3 taught that even with no hi, half the pool is outside the clean bowl and visible as word-shuffled and letter-scrambled, so a conservative 0.5 × lo guard should remove most of it, and since the budget is only 2T, even a half-size clean set can be learned twice as much as the fuller, dusty set of attempts 6 and 7.
outcome: dev 1.9015 against 1.8826 for the best at the time, rejected

idea: Add a domain-calibrated dedup guard instead of a raw-token cut-over. (1) Exact/near-duplicate removal exactly as in attempt 7 (hash of the lowercased, whitespace-normalised first 2000 chars, keep the first copy only). (2) Fragument-level safe-score: build the set of lowercased adjacent character bigrams of target_sample's first 8000 chars; for each pool doc, compute the fraction of its first 8000 chars that map to that set, and multiply it by the fraction of its next 5000 chars that map to it. This is the score attempt 3 used and is not doctored away by the single-pass order check. (3) Calibrate with a half-half leave-out over the 200 target docs, and set lo at the 2.5th-95th percentile midpoint. Split the kept docs into A and B by hash of the first 200 chars as in attempt 5. (4) Score a seeded 2000-doc random pool sample with the full 2.5th-95th midpoint lo as the only rule, and let hi be the same value. (5) Logistic-Regression simulation exactly as in the baseline: w = (200 × 1.0 + 2000 × neg_mean_h) / 2200, with positives = the 100 target docs each weighted twice (A once, B once), negatives = the seeded sample, and score = 1 / (1 + exp(-w × h)). Keep a doc if its score is at least the midpoint of the 5th percentile of the target scores (each doc scored twice) and the 95th percentile of the held-out pool scores. (6) Selection: start with all kept docs, then take docs in order of the selected list until about T tokens are reached; if the kept set holds fewer than T, let it cycle; if even the docs that pass the full lo guard hold fewer than T tokens, still let that cycle and do not top up with the next-highest-scoring docs, since attempt 3 (full lo, no hi, only kept docs, shuffled) beat attempts 6 and 7 with far fewer tokens and still cycled and did not fall back to off-domain text. (7) Shuffle with random.Random(int(os.environ.get('CURATE_SEED', 0))) and return the list. No split, no weights, nothing external.
why: Attempts 5 and 3 show that only clean, in-domain docs feed the target prior and that a raw cycle of them beats the half-butterfly, while attempts 6 and 7 lost once something was added, so try a fuller kept set with a second-order, end-scoring detox measured against the target's own leave-out gap, and feed just that until T, rather than padding with more unlabelled text.
